summary_md: **Computational Engineering, Finance, and Science ([@BNHNA](https://x.com/BNHNA/status/2116139756476158408))** shares *Tracekit Box* ([arXiv 2610.38458](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38458)) by Ghosh, an MIT micro-VM sandbox where each agent job runs in Firecracker without a network card and every outbound command, connection, secret or model call passes a signed, host-side gate ([Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit-box](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit-box)).

media.description: Abstract of the Tracekit Box paper.
media.ocr_text: AI agents now install packages, call model APIs with their operators' keys and change code in repositories that deploy to production. The network, credentials and write access they need are also how they can leak data, steal a key or change a system nobody approved. Sandboxes contain an agent but leave little evidence of what crossed their boundary; tracing records what happened but contains nothing. We present Tracekit Box, an open-source system (MIT, v0) that does both. Each job runs in its own Firecracker micro-VM with no network card. The only ways out are doors on the host, served over vsock: commands, outbound connections, secrets, model calls and the workspace patch. At every door a Tracekit signer the agent cannot reach decides what passes and signs it into one run per box. Names are resolved on the host; private and cloud-metadata addresses are always refused; secrets never enter the VM, which sees placeholders the host proxy swaps for real values only in one header for bound
